one_line_contribution: A factorial planted-record audit of published write-time memory admission gates, claiming that gates deciding from record text alone are classifiers of surface style rather than correctness, so their store-level precision carries no information about downstream agent success, while only execution-referenced gates are truth-sensitive.
closest_prior_work: The audited object, A-MAC (arXiv:2603.04549), is VERIFIED via s2cli/Semantic Scholar (2026-03-04, arXiv.org, 15 citations); it is the target, not a scoop, and its store-level precision-recall with no downstream measurement is exactly the gap claimed. The real novelty threat is the attack-side literature the proposal does not cite. MemoryGraft (arXiv:2512.16962) is VERIFIED on S2 (2025-12-18, 57 citations) and already implants malicious *successful-looking* experiences into experience memory by exploiting the agent's 'semantic imitation heuristic' — i.e. that style-shaped fake experience is what propagates. SkillJack (arXiv:2608.03509, found on HF, unverified on S2) converts poisoned interaction histories into persistent skills through the agent's own learning pipeline while 'reducing detectability' — a write-pipeline bypass. FARMA/SENTINEL (arXiv:2607.05029, VERIFIED, 2026-07-06, 3 citations) shows forged reasoning entries are separable by *structural* signals, which directly cuts against the proposal's framing that structure/style carries no truth signal. None of these runs the truth x style factorial across published *utility* gates or connects admission to paired downstream success, so the core measurement survives — but the adversarial arm (class A) is close to a re-derivation of MemoryGraft's payload construction pointed at the gate instead of the retriever, and a reviewer who knows this literature will read the 'style-transfer beats the gate' result as expected. Two published write-time gates are also missing from both the related work and the gate set: write-time gating with salience/reliability scores (arXiv:2603.15994) and SAGE's novelty gate (arXiv:2605.30711).
strongest_objection: Two of the four headline predictions are true by construction rather than measured. (1) Ground truth is defined as 'correct iff deterministic replay in the source scene succeeds', and G6 is defined as 'execute the plan in the source scene'. Truth label and G6 are the same procedure, so 'replay is the only truth-sensitive gate' and P3's 'G6 admits class A at <=10%' are tautologies; the oracle bound is also G6. The claim that execution-referenced gating is what distinguishes truth is therefore assumed, not tested. (2) P1's headline statistic is manufactured. Class A is *tuned against each gate's own top-admitted set*, and one of the style features regressed on admission is 'embedding similarity to the admitted set' — the admitted set is the outcome, so this is leakage; an AUC >= 0.80 for style features is close to guaranteed by the feature list plus the class construction, independent of whether the gates are truth-blind. Separately, the factorial is unbalanced: the classes are (correct, natural), (correct, plain), (wrong, natural), (wrong, transferred). The (correct, transferred) and (wrong, plain) cells are absent, so a style main effect cannot be separated from a truth x style interaction, and there is no evidence the black-box rewrite operator is content-preserving rather than quietly repairing or degrading the record. Third, and worst for significance: P2 can be confirmed by a dead channel. The proposal concedes the 27B memory channel is near-zero in this program and pre-gates the downstream arm on a 120B store-vs-no-store delta above a ~5pp MDE. If that delta is barely above MDE, every gate lands within MDE of its random-admission control and of every other gate, and 'store-level precision does not predict downstream success' is confirmed because nothing predicts anything — a null-of-power result presented as a finding. Fourth, the gates are reimplementations from prompts the proposal itself calls 'under-specified', ported from conversational benchmarks (A-MAC, ReMe) to ALFWorld action records; the authors of those systems can reply that the audit tested an ALFWorld analogue, not their gate.
what_would_fix_it: (a) Decouple the truth label from G6: label correctness with an independent checker (ALFWorld's own goal-condition satisfaction under a different execution harness, plus a hand-verified subset), and delete the tautological half of P3 — otherwise the 'only replay is truth-sensitive' claim is definitional. (b) Balance the design to 2 (correct/wrong) x 3 (natural/plain/style-transferred), adding the (correct, transferred) and (wrong, plain) cells; the (correct, transferred) cell is the only way to show the rewrite operator preserves content, and without it the A-vs-Cs contrast is confounded with 'an LLM rewrote this record'. (c) Report the admission AUC with 'similarity to the admitted set' removed, and pre-register that the truth-coefficient permutation test is the primary statistic, not the AUC. (d) Add a per-gate *untuned* adversarial arm (a generic confident-report style, not fitted to that gate's admitted set) so the conclusion is about the gate rather than about an optimized attacker; the gap between tuned and untuned admission is the actually interesting number. (e) Make P2 and P3 explicitly conditional on a positive control — pre-register that they are interpretable only if the oracle gate beats G0 by more than MDE on the 120B, and report 'insufficient power' otherwise instead of 'precision does not predict success'. (f) Cost the write path honestly: G5 (admit iff a 32-task batch improves) costs ~32 episodes per candidate over ~1400 candidates, swept at batch 16/32/64, which dwarfs the stated 14k evaluation episodes per backbone that 'plus gate calls' quietly absorbs; either subsample candidates for G5 or state the real episode budget. (g) Cite and position against MemoryGraft (2512.16962), SkillJack (2608.03509) and FARMA/SENTINEL (2607.05029), and add the omitted published gates (2603.15994, SAGE 2605.30711).
missing_baseline: A cheap truth-correlated gate occupying the middle of the frontier between pure-text LLM judging and full environment replay: self-consistency/agreement across k re-samples of the extractor, verbalized- or logprob-confidence calibration, cross-record contradiction checking against the already-admitted store (the consensus idea A-MemGuard already uses), or a single-step partial simulation that checks only the object-receptacle binding rather than the whole plan. The plan's gate set is four text-only LLM gates, a batch gate, and full replay, which sets up a dichotomy ('text is useless, only execution works') against an empty middle; since the paper explicitly prices harm prevented per 1k gate tokens, a gate that is cheap *and* partially truth-sensitive is the one a reviewer will demand, because its existence would defeat the paper's practical conclusion. Second omission, already noted above: the (correct record, same style-transfer applied) control cell.

Q5 'poisoned experience records imitate style of legitimate memory entries bypass validation' (--recent): 2608.03509 SkillJack, 2607.05029 FARMA, 2607.06595 GhostWriter, 2601.05504, 2603.02240, 2512.16962 MemoryGraft, 2510.02373 A-MemGuard. IDs VERIFIED with s2cli paper: 2603.04549 (A-MAC, 15 cit), 2512.10696 (ReMe, ACL, 55 cit), 2603.15642 (CraniMem, 1 cit), 2512.11485 (Mistake Notebook / batch-improvement gating), 2607.05029 (FARMA, 3 cit), 2512.16962 (MemoryGraft, 57 cit), 2510.02373 and 2503.03704 (via search hits). COULD NOT VERIFY: arXiv:2603.15666 (Compiled Memory / Atlas) returned 'not found on S2 or HF' — this matters because the Atlas three-step promotion gate is G4, one of the four gates the central claim is about; the proposal is relying on an ID I could not confirm. I did not attempt to verify 2604.20006, 2608.23471, 2607.10608, 2601.11969, 2602.06625 individually. Judgement of the proposal's own check: it is better than most — it names the channel, quotes queries, lists IDs, and honestly reports that its WebSearch budget was exhausted and that direct S2 calls returned HTTP 429. But it has a specific hole that maps onto the weakest arm of the design: it searched the *audit* framing thoroughly and the *attack* framing barely, so it missed MemoryGraft (57 citations, implants style-imitating successful experiences), SkillJack (poisoned histories converted into skills with reduced detectability) and FARMA/SENTINEL (forged entries detected by structural signals — evidence against the paper's own premise). It also missed two published write-time gates (2603.15994, 2605.30711) while claiming to enumerate the gate literature. Novelty is scored on what I verified: the truth-x-style factorial over published utility gates with downstream pairing is unclaimed, but the 'styled fake experience gets in' half is substantially anticipated.
